hook: What happens after a creator receives an enquiry?
body:
Content brings people into a conversation. Someone still needs to understand the question, answer accurately and return to it when more information is needed.

For a coach selling a cohort, that can mean checking fit, explaining the schedule and making sure a promise matches the actual offer. A program link alone may not settle those questions.

DealDock is being built around this part of the workflow. The product hypothesis is that creators with recurring commerce enquiries need clearer attention and review, alongside useful drafting support.

This is a product under validation. A possible opportunity is not a confirmed sale.
cta: What part of handling enquiries takes the most judgment in your business?

hook: An enquiry-handling tool needs the right customer.
body:
Creators face different problems. Some need a clearer offer or more relevant distribution. Others already receive serious enquiries and struggle to keep the conversations moving.

Those situations should not lead to the same software recommendation.

Before a DealDock research walkthrough, the useful questions are practical: What do you sell? Do purchase questions already arrive in Instagram DMs? What becomes difficult after the first question? What does your current routine handle well?

If the existing routine is sufficient, that is a useful result of the conversation.

hook: A handoff checklist for a creator and an assistant
body:
When someone else helps with the inbox, the next reply needs context. A simple handoff can include:

1. The question the person actually asked.
2. Accurate offer details and availability.
3. Any promise already made.
4. The person responsible for the next response.
5. Who reviews the message before sending.
6. Whether a completed sale has actually been confirmed.

This is a practical operating checklist, not a claim that every collaboration feature is live in DealDock.

hook: Keep estimated opportunity separate from confirmed sales.
body:
A revenue-focused tool needs to make uncertainty understandable. A conversation can look promising before someone decides to purchase.

If a value is estimated, label it as estimated. If a sale is confirmed by the creator, show that as a distinct outcome. Neither an unread message nor an estimate proves revenue was lost or recovered.

DealDock demonstrations should make this distinction visible. Any example shown before live validation uses clearly labelled sample data.

hook: What should an inbox tool prove before you pay for it?
body:
Start with one task you already do: recognizing a relevant enquiry, preparing an accurate response or returning to an unfinished conversation.

Compare the proposed tool with your existing workflow. Include the time to review drafts, the full cost, control over messages and what happens when the connection needs attention.

For DealDock, the next step is research with suitable creators and readiness-gated walkthroughs. A polished demonstration is an explanation of a workflow; live usefulness still needs evidence.
